en: The sampaguita, the national flower, was officially declared in 1934 by American Governor-General Frank Murphy.
Dr. Fe del Mundo became the first woman and first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School in 1936.
Doña Marcela Marino de Agoncillo and her daughters hand-sewed the first official Philippine flag in Hong Kong.
A Supreme Court justice in the Philippines must be at least forty years old with fifteen years of legal experience.
The Ifugao people engineered the Banaue Rice Terraces with an ancient irrigation system that still waters the crops today.
Before the Spanish arrived, many Filipinos wrote their own languages using the ancient pre-colonial Baybayin script.
National hero Jose Rizal was a polymath who could speak and write in twenty-two different languages.
During the Higantes Festival in Angono, locals parade giant paper puppets that can reach twelve feet tall.
The Philippine Constitution guarantees every child the right to free public education from elementary to high school.
The Filipino value of bayanihan originated from the tradition of neighbors carrying a whole nipa hut together.
Juan Luna won the first gold medal at the Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his Spoliarium painting.
The barangay is the smallest local government unit in the Philippines, originally named after the balangay boats.
